title: The PreToolUse scanner's heredoc-body opacity fix (#140): the refill-boundary bug class, and the $(/backtick hand-back tradeoff
content:
Landed at #140, merged to main as squash commit d041bb07f68fd378addfbf8b6d6530fb3bef6b58 (PR #144). This closed a real bypass of the blanket-staging PreToolUse gate (pre-tool-use.sh): an unbalanced quote inside a heredoc BODY leaked quote-state into the top-level scanner, because the redirection arm marked only the heredoc DELIMITER as a redirect target and never treated the body itself as an opaque region. Full run history (3 Phase 2 rounds, a Phase 2.5 design VETO and re-ruling, 2 Phase 3 rounds, 2 Phase 4 panel rounds, 2 additional scoped BA rulings) is at knowledge/issue-archive/140.json; this entry records the two lessons durable beyond this one fix.

LESSON 1 -- THE REFILL-BOUNDARY BUG CLASS. The scanner reads its input through a refilled/chunked window (the file's `_fill`/`_wordchunk` machinery, shared by every scanning path in the file, not just heredocs). The Phase 4 round-1 SecOps VETO found that the chosen design's heredoc-body-skip function (_hd_skip) set its 'line too long, give up matching' flag (_hdtoolong) whenever a heredoc body LINE merely straddled the scanner's internal refill/window boundary -- not only when the line genuinely exceeded a whole window, as the code's own comment claimed. When set, the terminator comparison for that line was suppressed, so body-opacity silently ran to end-of-command and a trailing `git add -A` after the (never-recognized) real terminator was allowed through. Measured on a completely ordinary 1042-byte heredoc (no adversarial quote/expansion tricks): the gate allowed it, and a real bash/zsh/sh run (via a recording-git-shim) confirmed the trailing `git add -A` genuinely executed. Swept exposure ranged 0.52% to 24% depending on line-length/line-count shape -- not a rare corner case. None of the then-current 12 ACs constrained this term (mutation-proving `_hdtoolong=1 -> =0` passed every AC row while changing live-input behavior). THE GENERALISABLE LESSON: any scanner or parser that reads through a chunked/refilled buffer needs its correctness property stated over BODY LENGTHS SPANNING MULTIPLE REFILL PERIODS, not just over content shapes -- a 'genuinely too long' condition and a 'not yet fully buffered' condition are easy to conflate in a single flag, and a fixture population built only from short/single-chunk inputs will never exercise the difference. The fix (incremental prefix matching that grows one refill chunk at a time and locks on first mismatch, replacing the coarse too-long flag) was verified with a real gate-bites proof: the exact unconditional-mismatch mutation was planted, the new >=1100-consecutive-body-length sweep (spanning >=2 full window periods) reddened, then reverted via `git checkout` (never a hand-edit) and reconfirmed green. Anyone touching _hd_skip, _fill, or _wordchunk again should re-run that sweep, not just the per-AC fixture cells -- see spec.json AC13 in the #140 archive for the exact property statement.

LESSON 2 -- THE $(/BACKTICK HAND-BACK TRADEOFF IS A COARSE, DELIBERATE, NOW-PINNED CHOICE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. AC12 makes an UNQUOTED heredoc introducer deny outright if the body contains a literal `$(`, backtick, or (originally) `${` before the real terminator -- a coarse 'deny on sighting' guard, not real tokenization. Three follow-up issues track its known edges, all deliberately accepted rather than fixed in #140 because a narrow fix would require real tokenization, which SecOps's round-3 VETO explicitly rejected as more than the minimum: (a) #145 -- bare backtick command substitution is NOT narrowed to a $(- style hand-back (backtick is not a structural character in the file's _STRUCT set at all, unlike '(' which lets $( safely hand back to ordinary top-level scanning); narrowing it would need real tokenization. IMPORTANT: #145's own proposed remedy (give backtick a $(-style hand-back) would IMPORT the gap in (b) below into the one arm currently immune to it -- do not implement #145 as originally written without re-reading this. (b) #146 -- the $( arm's hand-back does not consume the scanner's quote-state (_sc), so ordinary top-level scanning resumes over the raw heredoc body after a `$(...)` and an odd quote later in that same unquoted body re-enters the exact quote-parity regime #140 exists to close (53-byte repro archived in #140's peer-review shard). Confirmed NOT a regression relative to pre-#140 main (both return 'none'), so it shipped as a disclosed/accepted limitation with 21 pinning (characterization) test rows added, not a Dev code fix. (c) bare `${...}` parameter expansion was NARROWED OUT of the AC12 trigger entirely during the Phase 2.5 re-ruling -- verified live that bare `${...}` cannot itself execute a command, and any $(/backtick nested inside `${...}` is still independently caught by the unmodified raw-text scan; a QA mutation-battery finding that `${` had zero live coverage was thereby mooted (the check was removed, not left dead). THE GENERALISABLE LESSON: when a security control accepts a coarse rule over a narrow one specifically to avoid building a second tokenizer, PIN BOTH HALVES of that tradeoff with real assertions (what it catches AND what it deliberately still lets through), file the accepted gap as its own issue with a live, non-regression-confirmed repro, and cross-check any later 'fix' proposal for the sibling arm against the gap it might reopen -- exactly the #145-would-reimport-#146 trap found here.

STILL OPEN, NOT PART OF #140's SCOPE: #143 -- bare backtick command substitution (no heredoc at all) defeats the blanket-staging gate today, because backtick is not a structural character the scanner tracks; found by SecOps during #140's Phase 2.5 round as a separate, more severe, pre-existing bypass and filed rather than folded in. #147 -- a benign, Linux-CI-only performance-calibration margin narrowing in the AC7 density-discrimination guard (1.2x measured vs >1.2x required on the CI runner, 1.4x on the same commit on Darwin hosts), caused by routing more scanning through _hd_skip's length-dominated cost path; not a functional or security regression (absolute costs 140-181ms, the quadratic-blowup property that guard exists to catch was independently re-verified linear on Darwin by two separate Phase 4 rounds).
